newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kansai Elec says plans cost-cutting moves in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Kansai Elec says plans cost-cutting moves in 97/98.

text.p: Kansai Electric Power Co Inc will include fresh cost-cutting measures in its annual corporate management programme for fiscal 1997/98, starting on April 1, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
He quoted Kansai Electric president Yoshihisa Akiyama as saying the firm would draft a management programme by March to boost efficiency and include fresh cost-cutting measures.

The annual programme reviews the past fiscal year and outlines the company's plans for the coming business year. Japanese electric utilities are being pressed by the government to cut rates to levels comparable to overseas utilities.
This would require the industry to cut electricity rates by about 20 percent.
Akiyama said the company needed to take drastic measures to cut costs, the spokesman said.

Despite the calls that they cut rates, Japan's electric utility companies have decided to raise rates in April and May, citing rising fuel costs and the scheduled rise in the consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1.
The 10 major power utility companies will increase electricity rates for the average household by between 35 yen and 95 yen per month from April to reflect higher fuel costs.
They will raise rates again by another 130 yen to 140 yen from May because of the rise in consumption tax.
